summary: Learn geospatial AI workflows, classification, validation, and reporting. Build practical spatial intelligence skills in 5 days.
lede: Geospatial AI and location intelligence combines spatial data, imagery, and machine-learning methods to support planning and operational decisions. For professionals who work with maps, imagery, and location-based questions, the course covers preparing raster and vector data, engineering spatial features, and building supervised classification workflows. Participants also learn to assess model accuracy with confusion matrices and accuracy metrics, analyze land-cover change, and present findings through maps, dashboards, and briefings.
audienceIntro: This course is built for professionals who already work with spatial data and need to turn that work into stronger analysis, clearer decisions, and more reliable reporting. It suits people who manage maps, imagery, field data, and location-based performance questions in operational settings.
audience: Urban and Regional Planner using geospatial evidence
Operations Manager using dashboarded location intelligence
prerequisites: Recommended prerequisites: working knowledge of GIS concepts, basic raster and vector data handling, and familiarity with spatial layers, maps, and tabular datasets. Prior exposure to QGIS, ArcGIS, Google Earth Engine, or Python is helpful but not mandatory for conceptual participation. No programming is required to complete the course, although some modules introduce Python-enabled spatial workflows and AI-assisted geospatial analysis at an operational level. Participants should bring a laptop capable of running a browser-based GIS environment and working with spreadsheets and map files. A sample geospatial dataset will be provided for hands-on exercises.
topics: Generative AI at work & AI copilots
